result_text:
**The data does not show that the /lp/summer-sale launch improved checkout conversion, and it can't give a number for the campaign's effect.** Overall conversion was flat to slightly lower, and the campaign page converts far worse than the rest of the site.

**Numbers** (sessions to checkout, with 95% intervals):
- **Overall rate:** 3.12% before the launch (06-01 to 06-07) and 2.55% after (06-08 to 06-12). The change is −0.57 points, with an interval of −1.29 to +0.16. That is no detectable change, not an improvement. I dropped 06-13 and 06-14 because their session data is incomplete.
- **Campaign page:** 6 checkouts from 1,053 sessions (0.57%), against 3.04% for /home and /product. The gap is −2.47 points, with an interval of −3.17 to −1.76. It holds on both desktop and mobile.
- **Other traffic:** about 600 sessions a day throughout, converting at 3.04% against 3.12% before. The campaign traffic looks additive rather than cannibalising, but I observed that volume stability and didn't test it.
- **Net effect:** the campaign added about 160 sessions a day and roughly 6 checkouts in the week, against about 19 orders a day overall.

**Why no effect number:**
- **No comparison group:** the launch wasn't randomized and there was no holdout, so there is nothing to show what would have happened without it.
- **Concurrent release:** the v3.4.1 checkout form refactor shipped on 06-10, inside the post-launch window. With only two post-launch days before it, my data can't exclude a refactor effect of about 1 point either way.
- **06-13 and 06-14 gap:** mobile sessions fall from about 420 to about 245 a day on every page, while orders stay normal. On 06-01 to 06-12, orders match checkout-reached sessions exactly each day. On 06-13 and 06-14 there are 12 more orders than recorded checkouts (23 vs 17, then 17 vs 11), so mobile sessions are missing. I couldn't tell whether they went unrecorded or the export was incomplete.

**Not covered:** orders have no session ID, so I can't attribute any order to the campaign page. The window is only two weeks, with no seasonality control. A holdout or staggered rollout would give a real effect estimate.

Both the data-gap hypothesis and the "campaign traffic converts differently" hypothesis came out as best supported. The campaign-effect and refactor hypotheses stay unresolved. The ledger passed the structural validator after I fixed one slot label.
